name: 66. Databricks Model Serving and Unity AI Gateway surfaces
description:
Databricks serves foundation models on two surfaces under one workspace host, and the databricks provider
picks between them per request:

  /serving-endpoints          Foundation Model APIs - pay-per-token and provisioned-throughput endpoints,
                              addressed by endpoint name (databricks-claude-sonnet-4-5). Also serves the
                              OpenAI Responses API at /serving-endpoints/responses.
  /ai-gateway/mlflow/v1       Unity AI Gateway model services, addressed by Unity Catalog name
                              (system.ai.claude-sonnet-4-5, or <catalog>.<schema>.<service>).

Production path: POST /v1/chat/completions -> core/providers/databricks/inference.go -> prepareRequest ->
buildURL (databricks.go) -> openai.HandleOpenAI*Request. resolveAPIFormat is what chooses the base path:
an explicit api_format on the key wins, otherwise a dotted model name selects the AI Gateway and anything
else selects Model Serving.

Both surfaces are plain OpenAI wire format, so there are no Databricks-specific converters - which is
exactly why the routing needs pinning here. A regression in resolveAPIFormat or basePathFor does not fail
a converter unit test; it sends a valid request to the wrong base path and comes back 404 from a surface
that has never heard of the model. Cases 1 and 2 are that pair: the same workspace, the same credentials,
two model names that must land on different paths.

FIXTURE CONSTRAINT - the model names carry the routing signal. system.ai.claude-sonnet-4-5 must keep its
dots (they are what selects the AI Gateway) and databricks-claude-sonnet-4-5 must stay dot-free. Renaming
either to a 'cleaner' id silently stops testing the routing rule.
